_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Chad covering Sahelian rock art, Sao civilisation, Kanem-Bornu Empire, Wadai and Bagirmi sultanates, French conquest, Tombalbaye, Libyan-Chadian conflict, Déby dynasty, and the Lake Chad environmental crisis.

ethnic_groups.name: Sara
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; southern Chad; predominantly Christian; agriculturalists; multiple sub-groups (Nar, Madjingay, Mbay, Goulaye)

ethnic_groups.name: Arab (Chadian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Semi-nomadic and settled communities across the Sahel; Baggara cattle herders; Chadian Arabic

ethnic_groups.name: Kanembu/Kanuri
ethnic_groups.notes: Around Lake Chad; historical Kanem-Bornu Empire heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Wadai/Maba
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Chad; Wadai Sultanate heritage; Abéché region

ethnic_groups.name: Gorane/Toubou
ethnic_groups.notes: Saharan north including Tibesti; Teda and Daza subgroups; Déby's ethnic base (Zaghawa subgroup)

ethnic_groups.name: Zaghawa
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern border with Sudan; Déby family's ethnic group; cross-border ties with Darfur

ethnic_groups.name: Massa/Moussei
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Chad; Mayo-Kebbi region; fishing and farming

ethnic_groups.name: Hadjerai
ethnic_groups.notes: Guéra massif peoples; diverse mountain communities; include Kenga, Dangaléat, Migami

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul
ethnic_groups.notes: Semi-nomadic cattle pastoralists across the Sahel

ethnic_groups.name: Kotoko
ethnic_groups.notes: Far northern Cameroon border; Sao civilisation successors; city-state heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Bulala
ethnic_groups.notes: Fitri Lake region; historically challenged Kanem dynasty

current_leader.name: Mahamat Idriss Déby
current_leader.title: President (formerly Transitional Military Council chairman)
current_leader.notes: Son of Idriss Déby; took power after father's death; won disputed 2024 election

former_leaders.name: François (Ngarta) Tombalbaye
former_leaders.notes: First president; Sara southerner; assassinated in military coup

former_leaders.name: Félix Malloum
former_leaders.notes: Military head of state; failed to end civil war

former_leaders.name: Goukouni Oueddei
former_leaders.notes: GUNT leader; invited Libyan troops; ousted by Habré

former_leaders.name: Hissène Habré
former_leaders.notes: Overthrew Goukouni; Toyota War victor; DDS secret police killed 40,000; convicted of crimes against humanity 2016

former_leaders.name: Idriss Déby
former_leaders.notes: 30-year rule; Zaghawa; oil era; counterterrorism partner; killed on frontlines April 2021

910.name: Saharan Rock Art and Early Peoples
910.description: The Ennedi and Tibesti massifs preserve stunning Saharan rock art depicting a green Sahara; pastoralist and agricultural communities thrive before desertification.

sub_clusters.name: Ennedi and Tibesti Rock Art
sub_clusters.description: Rock paintings and engravings in the Ennedi Plateau and Tibesti Mountains show cattle herding, hunting, and ritual scenes from the African Humid Period.

sub_clusters.name: Green Sahara Desiccation and Migration
sub_clusters.description: Sahara dries out; populations migrate southward to the Lake Chad basin and Sahel; foundation for later sedentary civilisations.

910.name: Sao Civilisation
910.description: The Sao people build walled settlements around Lake Chad; terracotta and bronze artistic traditions; eventually absorbed by Kanem-Bornu.

sub_clusters.name: Sao Walled Settlements and Art
sub_clusters.description: Sao communities construct mound settlements in the Lake Chad floodplain; renowned terracotta figurines and funerary traditions.

sub_clusters.name: Sao Absorption into Kanem-Bornu
sub_clusters.description: Kanem Empire gradually incorporates Sao communities; Kotoko city-states emerge as Sao successor polities.

920.name: Kanem Empire
920.description: The Kanem Empire, ruled by the Saifawa dynasty, dominates the Lake Chad region; Islam adopted c.1085; trans-Saharan trade flourishes.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of the Saifawa Dynasty
sub_clusters.description: Duguwa and Saifawa rulers unite Kanem; control of trans-Saharan trade routes linking Fezzan and the Nile Valley.

sub_clusters.name: Islamisation of Kanem
sub_clusters.description: Mai Hummay adopts Islam c.1085; Kanem becomes a centre of Islamic learning; diplomatic links with North Africa and Egypt.

sub_clusters.name: Kanem Expansion and Bulala Challenge
sub_clusters.description: Kanem reaches greatest extent under Mai Dunama Dibalami; Bulala attacks force Saifawa retreat westward to Bornu.

920.name: Bornu Empire
920.description: The Saifawa dynasty re-establishes power west of Lake Chad as the Bornu Empire; Idris Alooma's golden age; gradual decline.

sub_clusters.name: Bornu Renaissance under Idris Alooma
sub_clusters.description: Mai Idris Alooma modernises the army with firearms; diplomatic ties with Ottoman Tripoli; Bornu recaptures Kanem heartland.

sub_clusters.name: Bornu Decline and Rabih az-Zubayr
sub_clusters.description: Fulani jihad pressures Bornu; El-Kanemi sheikhs supplant Saifawa; Rabih az-Zubayr conquers Bornu 1893; end of millennium-old dynasty.

930.name: Wadai and Bagirmi Sultanates
930.description: The Sultanate of Wadai and the Kingdom of Bagirmi emerge as major powers east and south of Lake Chad; slave trading and Islamic culture.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Bagirmi
sub_clusters.description: Bagirmi kingdom centered on Massenya; vassal to Bornu then Wadai; slave raiding in the south; French conquest 1897.

sub_clusters.name: Sultanate of Wadai
sub_clusters.description: Wadai sultanate centred on Abéché; controls Saharan trade routes to Benghazi; defeats Bornu influence; last independent sultanate falls to France 1912.

940.name: French Conquest and Colonial Chad
940.description: France conquers Chad in stages; Territoire Militaire du Tchad within AEF; forced cotton cultivation in the south; Félix Éboué rallies Chad to Free France.

sub_clusters.name: French Conquest and Battle of Kousséri
sub_clusters.description: Three French columns converge and defeat Rabih at Kousséri (1900); progressive pacification of the north; last Senoussi resistance 1920.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Exploitation: Le Tchad Utile
sub_clusters.description: France develops only 'le Tchad utile' (useful south); forced cotton cultivation; Muslim north neglected; Éboué rallies Chad to Free France 1940; post-war political awakening.

sub_clusters.name: Félix Éboué and Free France
sub_clusters.description: Governor Éboué makes Chad first colony to join Free France August 1940; Leclerc's column departs from Faya-Largeau; Chad's strategic role in WWII.

950.name: Independence and Tombalbaye Era
950.description: François (Ngarta) Tombalbaye leads independence; southern Christian domination; northern Muslim rebellion (FROLINAT); increasing authoritarianism and assassination.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and One-Party Rule
sub_clusters.description: Chad independent 11 August 1960; Tombalbaye's PPT becomes sole party; southern-dominated government alienates the Muslim north.

sub_clusters.name: FROLINAT Northern Rebellion
sub_clusters.description: Front de Libération Nationale du Tchad (FROLINAT) launches insurgency; French military intervention (Operation Bison); Tombalbaye assassinated in military coup April 1975.

950.name: Civil Wars and Libyan Intervention
950.description: Chadian civil wars intensify; Libya annexes the Aouzou Strip; Habré and Goukouni factions clash; Toyota War drives out Libyan forces.

sub_clusters.name: Malloum, Habré, and Goukouni Power Struggles
sub_clusters.description: General Malloum overthrown; Goukouni's GUNT vs Habré's FAN; Libyan troops invited then expelled; Habré seizes N'Djamena 1982.

sub_clusters.name: Libyan-Chadian Conflict and Toyota War
sub_clusters.description: Gaddafi's Libya occupies Aouzou Strip and intervenes repeatedly; Toyota War (1987) sees Chad rout Libyan forces using pickup trucks; ICJ awards Aouzou to Chad 1994.

sub_clusters.name: Habré Regime and DDS Repression
sub_clusters.description: Hissène Habré rules through secret police (DDS); estimated 40,000 killed; later convicted of crimes against humanity in Senegal.

960.name: Déby Dynasty and Contemporary Chad
960.description: Idriss Déby seizes power 1990; 30-year rule; oil revenues; regional military power; killed in battle 2021; son Mahamat Déby takes over.

sub_clusters.name: Idriss Déby's Rise and Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Déby overthrows Habré December 1990; multiparty constitution 1996; eliminates term limits; oil pipeline to Cameroon opens 2003.

sub_clusters.name: Oil Revenues and Regional Power
sub_clusters.description: Doba oil fields transform economy; World Bank transparency experiment fails; Chad becomes key French and US counterterrorism partner in Sahel.

sub_clusters.name: Idriss Déby Death and Mahamat Succession
sub_clusters.description: Idriss Déby killed visiting frontlines April 2021; military council installs son Mahamat Idriss Déby; contested transition; October 2022 protests violently suppressed.

sub_clusters.name: Lake Chad Environmental and Security Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Lake Chad shrinks dramatically; humanitarian crisis affecting millions; Boko Haram attacks on Chadian shores; food insecurity and displacement.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
